Subject: Catalyze intro — 30-min product walkthrough & stakeholder timeblocks

Hi Emily / Samir —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap from our discovery: Catalyze is evaluating options to reduce per-request latency for conversational retrieval use cases and wants predictable inference costs across dev and prod. Key success criteria you called out were sub-200ms tail latency for short queries, clear data isolation controls, and a rollout path that supports a pilot with 2–3 internal teams.

Next step: we recommend a 30-minute walkthrough (high-level product demo + how Redwood would map to your pilot) with the following goals:
- Show the runtime and latency profiles on representative queries
- Walk through deployment options (Hosted vs. Dedicated vs. Private) and security controls
- Quick discussion of timeline and pilot milestones

Proposed 30-minute windows (ET) — please indicate which works best and who will attend (roles):
A) Tue Dec 8, 11:00–11:30 AM ET
B) Wed Dec 9, 3:00–3:30 PM ET
C) Thu Dec 10, 9:00–9:30 AM ET

Suggested stakeholders to include (2–3 people):
- Decision maker / Product owner
- Engineering lead (infra/ML)
- Security/compliance or SOC/Privacy reviewer (if available)

I can run the product portion; Alex will lead any technical deep-dive. I attached a brief agenda and one-pager to help stakeholders prepare. If none of these slots fit, tell me two windows and we’ll accommodate.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning calendars.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
